s18.router_note: Prefill instances on 2 H100s (decode instances keep 4), every split that uses all 24 GPUs; otherwise as section 17 (TTFT SLO 2,821 ms). A whole Llama-3-70B shape only just fits on two H100s (section 16: KV room for one 8,192-token batch); the CED encoder fits with 25x the room. The roofline charges no extra cost for a tight fit, so this compares capacity, not feasibility. The decoder-only row is limited by the prefill router, not by compute: the router (unchanged) sends each request to the instance with the fewest queued prompt tokens and ignores the batch in flight, so with 1.1-second steps it piles work onto busy instances while others idle. The same router applies in section 17, where it slightly favours the model with the shorter prefill steps.

quotes.s16_intro: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (arXiv:2609.19969, section 2.2) splits its 40 layers into a 20-layer causal encoder and a 20-layer decoder whose global KV is projected from the last encoder hidden state, so a prompt token runs only the encoder (and the decoder's K/V projections). The proxy here is the dense Llama-3-70B shape split 40 + 40 (`llama3-70b-ced`); the last 128 prompt tokens are replayed through the decoder (the paper's n_win = 128), on the prefill instance (`--ced-replay-on prefill`, the paper) or as the decode instance's first step (`--ced-replay-on decode`, SGLang RFC #39963, where a prefill instance holds only the encoder). Decode always runs the whole model. Illustrative: the paper's model is a 552B MoE with compressed sparse attention.
quotes.s16_paper: The paper's own figures are 8B activated per token at prefill and 16B at decode (abstract; section 4.2.1).
quotes.s17_intro: Highest Poisson rate with at least 90% of requests inside both SLOs (bisection on full runs to 2%, as `search.max_sustainable_rate`), for every split of 6 instances into prefill and decode pools. 1000 requests, seed 1, prompt and output cv 0.5, InfiniBand NDR, TPOT SLO 25 ms; TTFT SLO = 5x the decoder-only model's unloaded prefill of the mean prompt (shown). The prompt:output ratios stand in for agent loops (illustrative). Gains above 2x are queueing, not FLOPs: with a fixed TTFT SLO, halving the prefill service time cuts the queueing delay by more than half.
